title: Lesson 46: Data Pipelines for RAG: ETL, Connectors, CDC, and Incremental Refresh
description: A RAG pipeline is ETL wearing an AI costume: extract from connectors, transform raw records into clean text, and load chunks into a vector store. This lesson covers connector style (pull versus push), normalizing data before it reaches the embedding model, change data capture, and incremental refresh that re-embeds only what changed.

questions.question: Why should raw source records be normalized before they reach the embedding model?
options: Raw payloads waste embedding budget on structural noise and dilute attention, producing low-quality vectors
Normalization allows the embedding model to choose all of its own chunk boundaries directly from the raw source text
Normalization removes the need to chunk the text because the model handles whole documents
The embedding model can reliably separate the semantic signal from syntax without any help
questions.explanation: The embedding model cannot tell meaning from syntax, so structural noise consumes the token budget and pulls attention away from the text that carries the semantic signal.

questions.question: What does change data capture let a retrieval pipeline do?
options: Re-embed the entire corpus on every single run so that the index is always perfectly consistent and current
Replace the embedding model entirely with a fixed set of deterministic rules and mappings
See an event for each insert, update, and delete, so it can re-embed only the content that changed
Avoid needing a vector store at all by serving results directly from the source system
questions.explanation: Capturing change as a stream of insert, update, and delete events tells the pipeline exactly what moved, which is what makes it possible to re-embed only those records.

questions.question: Why must a retrieval pipeline handle deletions as a first-class operation?
options: Deleting a record in the connected source system always removes all of that record's derived vectors automatically
A source delete does not propagate on its own, so without a delete path the removed content stays retrievable
Deletions only matter when the vector store itself is the source of truth for the data
Deletion is handled automatically by the embedding model during the next scheduled pipeline run
questions.explanation: Because the vector store is separate from the source, a deletion has to be propagated explicitly or the derived chunks linger and remain retrievable after the source is gone.
